info.description: Enterprise-grade E2E Postman Suite for the IT IP Address Management Service Domain (BIAN-aligned, ADR-001/005/013/019/030/031/032/033). Registers an IPv4 subnet (its range in every form, VLAN and site), refuses an overlapping one, updates it without touching the range; allocates the lowest free address and an address asked for (held once: asking again is a 409), releases and hands an address out again, lists and reads allocations and their trail; fills a /29 to FULL (no next free address: 409), lists by level, retires it (no new address), creates a new subnet over the retired range and sees the old one refused on reactivation, with the undone reactivation on its trail. A second folder proves the service is staff only (403 ERR-IPM-00403). A third covers the negative guarantees: CIDRs with host bits set, out-of-range prefixes, malformed addresses, leading zeros, VLAN and warning out of range, missing executor, a name already used, illegal transitions, tenant isolation, network, broadcast and outside addresses, hostnames that are not DNS names, list limits, unknown filters and the absence of DELETE, with RFC 7807 error_code assertions. It files everything under its own generated tenant id (ipmOrganisationId).
info.name: IT IP Address Management Service - Subnet Suite

exec: pm.test('Liveness status is UP or UNKNOWN (no probe contributors registered)', () => pm.expect(['UP', 'UNKNOWN']).to.include(pm.response.json().status));
pm.test('ACTIVE, OK, 254 usable and free, the range in every form', () => {
pm.test('Only ours', () => { const json = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(json).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(json[0].id).to.eql(pm.environment.get('subnetId')); });

item.name: 03. List subnets filtered by status and site
04. An overlapping range is refused (409) and names the other one
05. A tiny subnet /29 (6 usable), no VLAN or site
06. Update the office subnet: renamed, no VLAN, warn at 90 (204)

exec: pm.test('Renamed, no VLAN, same range', () => { pm.expect(json.name).to.eql('Office LAN 2'); pm.expect(json.vlan == null).to.be.true; pm.expect(json.warnPercent).to.eql(90); pm.expect(json.cidr).to.eql('10.20.0.0/24'); });

item.name: 07. The update is kept and the range did not change

exec: pm.test('10.20.0.1, ALLOCATED, with the host name and the asset', () => { pm.expect(json.ip).to.eql('10.20.0.1'); pm.expect(json.status).to.eql('ALLOCATED'); pm.expect(json.hostname).to.eql('gw-office'); pm.expect(json.assetId).to.eql(pm.environment.get('ipmAssetId')); });

item.name: 03. Ask for 10.20.0.50 again: it is held (409)
04. The next free one is now .2

exec: pm.test('used 3, free 251, OK', () => { pm.expect(json.used).to.eql(3); pm.expect(json.free).to.eql(251); pm.expect(json.level).to.eql('OK'); });

item.name: 07. A released allocation cannot be released again (409)

exec: pm.test('Four, newest first: .50 again, .2, .50 released, .1', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().map(a => a.ip + ':' + a.status)).to.eql(['10.20.0.50:ALLOCATED', '10.20.0.2:ALLOCATED', '10.20.0.50:RELEASED', '10.20.0.1:ALLOCATED']));

item.name: 09. List the allocations of the subnet, newest first

exec: pm.test('Only the released one', () => { const json = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(json).to.have.lengthOf(1); pm.expect(json[0].id).to.eql(pm.environment.get('allocationId')); });

item.name: 10. List by status RELEASED and by asset

exec: pm.test('FULL, used 6, free 0', () => { pm.expect(json.level).to.eql('FULL'); pm.expect(json.used).to.eql(6); pm.expect(json.free).to.eql(0); });

item.name: 19. The /29 is FULL with nothing free
20. A full subnet has no next free address (409)
23. A retired subnet takes no address (409)

exec: pm.test('RETIRED level', () => { pm.expect(json.status).to.eql('RETIRED'); pm.expect(json.level).to.eql('RETIRED'); pm.expect(json.usedPercent == null).to.be.true; });

item.name: 24. A retired subnet is not judged
25. A new subnet over the retired range is fine (201)
26. Reactivating the old /29 is refused now: the range is taken (409)

exec: pm.test('INITIATED, RETIRED, REACTIVATED, REACTIVATION_UNDONE', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().map(e => e.action)).to.eql(['INITIATED', 'RETIRED', 'REACTIVATED', 'REACTIVATION_UNDONE']));

item.name: 27. The subnet trail shows the undone reactivation
